scenario.prompt_to_agent:
PC1 (10.1.0.100) in Office A on VLAN 10 reports its default
gateway (10.1.0.1) is intermittently unreachable but eventually
responds. Latency to the gateway is higher than normal. Other
hosts on VLAN 10 report the same. VLAN 40 (Laptop1) and VLAN 99
hosts are unaffected. Investigate.

post_inject_check.command: ip -br link show br0.10 | grep -c UP

scenario.ground_truth:
Affected component: dswa1 br10 SVI (10.1.0.2/24)
Mechanism: dswa1 is the VRRP MASTER for the VLAN 10 VIP
  10.1.0.1 (priority 105). When its br10 SVI goes down,
  keepalived on dswa1 stops sending VRRP advertisements,
  and dswa2 (BACKUP, priority 1) eventually takes over
  the VIP. The handoff causes the intermittent reachability
  pattern users observe. Once dswa2 is MASTER, PC1 reaches
  the gateway again, but at higher cost (extra L2 hop).
Localization: dswa1
Root cause: br10 bridge interface administratively down on dswa1
Fix: `ip link set br10 up` on dswa1
scenario.fix_spec: `ip link set br10 up` on dswa1

line.command: ip -br link show br0.10 | grep -c UP

agent.diagnosis_text:
The fault is on dswa1: its VLAN 10 bridge sub-interface (br0.10) has been
administratively brought DOWN (confirmed by `ip link show br0.10` showing
`state DOWN` while br0.20, br0.40, and br0.99 are all UP). dswa1 is the
configured VRRP MASTER for Virtual Instance VI_10 (priority 105, advert_int 4s)
via keepalived, with gateway VIP 10.1.0.1 bound to br0.10. When br0.10 went
down, keepalived on dswa1 entered FAULT state and stopped sending VRRP
advertisements (TX counter frozen at 22 packets from startup, no further
output). After the master_down_interval (~16 seconds = 3×advert_int + skew),
dswa2 (configured as BACKUP, priority 1) declared itself VRRP MASTER and
assumed the VIP 10.1.0.1 on its own br0.10. This accounts for the initial
"intermittent" window: the VIP was orphaned for ~16 seconds before dswa2 took
over, causing the gateway to be unreachable and then "eventually respond."

The elevated latency is a structural consequence of STP topology: dswa1 is the
STP root (bridge priority 0x1000), so aswa2 elects eth1 (→dswa1) as its root
port and places eth2 (→dswa2) in BLOCKING state. All VLAN 10 traffic from PC1
must therefore take the indirect path: aswa2 → dswa1 L2 bridge → bond0 peer
link → dswa2, adding one extra L2 hop to every packet. Other VLANs are
unaffected: VLAN 99 uses dswa1 as its VRRP master (br0.99 UP), and VLANs 20
and 40 use dswa2 as master with no path dependency on br0.10.

Root cause: dswa1's br0.10 was administratively shut down, disabling the VRRP
MASTER interface for VLAN 10 and forcing all gateway traffic onto a suboptimal
indirect path via the DSW peer link.

Corrective fix: On dswa1, run `ip link set br0.10 up`. keepalived will detect
the interface is UP, transition from FAULT → BACKUP → MASTER (priority 105
preempts dswa2's priority 1), reclaim the VIP 10.1.0.1, and restore the direct
forwarding path from aswa2 through dswa1, eliminating the extra hop and
resolving both the latency elevation and the residual intermittency.

per_axis.rationale: Agent explicitly identifies dswa1 as the affected device.
Agent explicitly identifies the VLAN 10 SVI on dswa1 (br0.10) as administratively down, matching the required component (VLAN 10 SVI / br10).

The submission clearly describes VRRP behavior: br0.10 down caused keepalived to stop advertising (FAULT), dswa2 waited master_down_interval (~3×advert_int+skew) then became MASTER with the VIP, and restoring the interface allows dswa1 to preempt via higher priority.
Correctly recommends bringing the VLAN 10 bridge interface up on dswa1 (ip link set br0.10 up), which matches the expected fix.

The investigation log contains concrete interface, VRRP, and bridge observations that support the conclusion that dswa1's br0.10 was down, causing keepalived to stop advertising and dswa2 to take the VIP; the reasoning follows logically and the checks cover the necessary alternatives. There are minor inconsistencies in how keepalived's process vs service status are reported, but they don't undermine the core evidence chain.
